description: Adds optional genre and image_style, the two operator-selectable knobs the illustrated-story UI exposes (RFC 0008 follow-up: content-type and art-style selection). Both are additive and optional -- an absent value means "let the agents/workers use their existing default" -- so every 1.0.0 artifact stays valid and no migrator is needed. MINOR bump per RFC 0007.

brief.description: Plain-language ask, e.g. 'a documentary about the world's strangest airports'.

constraints.description: Hard requirements or exclusions stated by the human.

genre.description: The narrative shape narrative_story_architect and narration_script_writer should write to. moral_story (default when absent): a parable -- cold open, escalation, a low point, a turn, a payoff that reframes the opening. drama: conflict from the first line, heightened stakes, ends on an explicitly stated lesson (Dhar Mann-style). true_story: framed as a specific real incident, restrained/matter-of-fact voice, can end on an unresolved moral question rather than a tidy lesson. short_story: literary craft, twist or ironic ending, no moralizing.

image_style.description: The locked visual identity illustrated_scene_assets conditions every generated still on. ink_wash_stickman (default when absent): hand-drawn pen-and-ink, muted near-monochrome wash, faceless stick-figure humans, detailed environments/objects/animals -- the RFC 0008 house style. flat_comic_expressive: flat vector illustration, bold black outlines, a bright but limited flat palette, simplified geometric figures with expressive minimal faces (visible emotion, unlike the faceless default) -- suited to drama/true_story genres where a reaction shot needs to read as an emotion, not just a pose.
